niche.habitat: Lower stratosphere haze layer and turbulent boundary interfaces where Astrophage aerosols suspend (F6), drifting in stable laminar flows (F18).
niche.diet: Astrophage particulates metabolized via enzymatic dissolution (F15); dissolved redox gradients accessed through ion-exchange membranes (F16).
niche.active: Diurnal; peaks during high irradiance when Astrophage flux is maximal (F6, F14), switching to chemo-mode in deep haze shadows (F16).

body: A gelatinous sphere of hygroscopic vesicles encased in a silica-reinforced lattice (F13), drifting like a microscopic dandelion in the amber haze (F8). Enzymatic pits line the surface to dissolve photoconductors (F15), while mucilage rafts ripple along the flanks to couple with low-frequency pressure waves in the dense air (F7).

journal.en: They eat the sky and float on the digestion.

skill.effect: The colony vibrates to draw nearby allies into a tight cluster, making them harder to scatter. This resonance only travels effectively through thick mist or damp earth.

journal.en: They dance to the world's low hum.
